sample_unit: documents (imaging reports, oncologist notes, discharge summaries)

links.outcome: Vulnerability of text classifiers trained on PHI to membership inference attacks
links.effect: Membership inference vulnerability was confirmed in text classification models trained directly on PHI. Teacher-student distillation onto public MIMIC-IV data was used to build shareable models.
links.quote: In this study, the vulnerability of text classification models trained directly on protected health information to membership inference attacks is confirmed.

unlisted_practices: Teacher-student distillation with private labeling of public datasets to create shareable clinical AI models

screen.reason: Empirically tests a teacher-student model distillation approach using public datasets to safeguard patient privacy against membership inference attacks prior to cross-institutional sharing.

primary.practice: teacher-student knowledge distillation for privacy preservation
